title: autonomous-cost-guardian: safe batching/caching config recommender with quality sentinels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a recommender + safe-apply pipeline that suggests batching and KV-caching profiles per route, validates quality using an automated eval harness ("quality sentinels"), and performs staged applies or automated rollback when regressions are detected. This ticket covers the engineering work to wire the recommender outputs into a CI-gated apply flow, extend the eval harness with new sentinel families, and create runbooked rollback criteria and dashboards.
context_and_background: We already have automated recommendations for batch/cache settings but lack defensible, automated quality checks before applying changes broadly. Prior tickets delivered recommendation engines and golden-prompt suites separately; this ticket glues them and codifies thresholds + rollout automation so cost savings can be applied safely without manual sample-and-hunch checks.
technical_scope: 1) Expand eval harness to support 'sentinel groups' (semantic anchors, structure checks, function-call fidelity). 2) Add a lightweight sampling layer to mirror production traffic to a shadow harness for deterministic comparison. 3) Integrate recommender -> CI pipeline: produce a candidate patch, run sentinels, and gate apply with statistical tests. 4) Implement canary rollout controller: 5%->20%->50%->100% with hold windows and automatic rollback triggers. 5) Dashboard + alerts for regressions and cost delta estimates.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender outputs per-route config JSON and expected cost delta estimate for tokens and GPU utilization.
Eval harness can run on sampled traffic and return a pass/fail per sentinel group within 30m for a 1k-sample job.
Default acceptance thresholds: embedding-similarity >= 0.94 (mean cosine), structured-output schema match >= 99%, hallucination indicator <= +1.5% relative to baseline, response-length drift < 10%.

Canary controller advances automatically when all sentinel groups pass and cost delta is within expected bounds; rolls back automatically on any critical sentinel failure or >2% absolute regression on primary metric with p<0.01.
Dashboard tile shows estimated monthly savings, observed saving during canary, and per-sentinel delta; alerts trigger to #infra-ops and on-call when auto-rollback occurs.
Documentation and runbook published: how to interpret sentinel results, manual override steps, and runbooked communication templates for customers when a rollback impacts latency/SLA.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for recommender output formatting and CI patch creation. 2) E2E test harness that replays 1k historical requests to compare baseline vs candidate with deterministic RNG seeds. 3) Canary simulation job (local CI) that simulates staged percentages and asserts that rollout controller halts/rolls back when thresholds breached. 4) Load smoke runs to validate no regressions in tail latency when batching/caching applied.
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): 5% internal routes for 24h (hold) -> Phase B (beta customers): 20% for 48h -> Phase C (general): 50% for 24h -> Full. Each phase blocked by all sentinel passes and no critical alerts in hold period. Manual 'force-apply' requires approval from ENG on-call + PM.
automatic_rollback_triggers: Critical sentinel fail (schema-breaking or function-call mismatch)
Primary metric absolute regression > 2% with p<0.01 over comparison sample
Observed end-to-end increase in 95th pct latency > 15% during canary
Unanticipated increase in error-rate (5xx) > 0.5 percentage points
monitoring_and_alerts: Create Grafana dashboard: per-route cost delta, mean embedding similarity, schema-match rate, hallucination indicator, tail latencies, error rates. Alert rules: page on any automatic rollback; page on primary metric regression; notify on minor sentinel drift.
implementation_notes: - Use statistically robust tests (bootstrap CIs) rather than simple means when sample sizes < 2k. - Shadow sampling should mask PII and follow KMS encryption rules. - Where candidate changes reduce token costs but change tokenization boundaries (e.g., by enabling prefix caching), make sure tokenizer-aware diffing is applied to avoid false-positive hallucination signals.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False alarms caused by non-deterministic sampling. Mitigation: use deterministic replay seeds and control traffic shaping for tests.
Risk: Over-aggressive batching increases tail latency. Mitigation: enforce latency SLO checks in canary; limit max-batch-size per route.
Risk: Silent quality drift for low-volume routes. Mitigation: mark low-volume routes as manual-approval-only and require weekly aggregated checks.
Risk: Operational confusion during rollback. Mitigation: publish communication templates and automated incident notes to Slack channel #infra-ops.
notes: PM feedback (2026-03-04): prefer embedding similarity + structured schema checks as primary sentinels for business-critical routes.
Design review (2026-03-06): agreed to surface expected cost delta and confidence score next to recommendation.
SRE review (2026-03-09): requested additional 95th/99th latency checks and a kill-switch feature to disable auto-applies for a tenant.
Next steps: merge PRs + schedule a 2-hour run with real traffic mirrors for Wednesday Canary kickoff.
